profile.headline: Software Engineer at Meta Reality Labs
profile.summary: Experienced Embedded Software Engineer. Skilled in C, C++, Python, Linux, and Robotics. Strong engineering professional with a Master of Science (MS) in Electrical and Computer Engineering focused in embedded systems and signal processing from Worcester Polytechnic Institute.

positions.title: Firmware Engineer
positions.description: Firmware development and support for the Embedded Linux-based Amazon Glow device. Bootloader, recovery, and thermal management experience.

positions.title: Firmware Engineer
positions.description:
Design and develop optimized C firmware for low power, memory constrained, real-time Bluetooth embedded devices in FreeRTOS environment. Worked on the Halo Band and Echo Loop.

* Assisted with line bring-up at our CM on multiple occasions, both on-site and remotely.
* Set up and maintained development pipeline from build to device provisioning.
* RTOS management and optimization to maximize battery life.
* Board bringup and crossfunctional debugging with EE team.

positions.title: Electronic Systems Development Engineer
positions.description: Full time position writing C++ and Python software with the satellite navigation team to enhance navigation filtering capabilities, allowing navigation filters to be thoroughly tested in a realistic simulation environment. I was responsible for the development and testing of a new filter evaluation framework for prototyping new techniques to detect and mitigate GPS vulnerabilities.

positions.title: Electronic Systems Development Intern
positions.description:
Summer 2016
I worked on PNT-Hub, an Army sponsored project creating a position, navigation, and timing hub for all Army land vehicles. My task, along with another intern, was to implement an algorithm for detecting when the vehicle is stationary based solely upon accelerometer and gyroscope readings. This is used to recalibrate the navigation filter when GPS is not available.

I was also a part of the second iteration of the embedded Capture the Flag competition for hardware security training. Working as a small team of interns, we successfully created a bootloader for an AVR microcontroller. The bootloader manages the start-up process and allows the code on the device to be updated by receiving and verifying encrypted firmware over the serial port.

positions.title: Electronic Systems Development Intern
positions.description:
Summer 2015
I worked on the application deployment system for the DARPA C2E Project helping develop a next-generation embedded system framework for military communications. I was heavily involved with the design and was responsible for the initial implementation of the deployment system.

Additionally, I participated in a one-of-a-kind embedded systems attack and defend style capture the flag competition with other interns. This was an extended multi-week project investigating security, especially implementation security, of an Internet Of Things style device.

positions.title: Sensor Systems Intern
positions.description:
Summer 2014
I worked on the MITRE Experimental Radar (MXR) project on the signal processing and exploitation team. I was responsible for making improvements, fixing bugs throughout the MATLAB code base, and creating demonstrations to show the functionality of the framework. I worked with a moderately sized team of developers and mathematicians to advance the state of the art in multistatic radar. MITRE's multistatic radar framework supported multiple branches of the US military.

positions.title: Information Security Intern
positions.description: I interned under the Chief Information Security Officer of the Commonwealth of Virginia multiple times over summer and winter breaks. I was responsible for optimizing multiple aspects of the department's vulnerability monitoring system. I set up and managed a new Ubuntu Linux server (including firewall rules and other system configuration) with Apache, MySQL, and Python to monitor and store vulnerability information. Other tasks included writing object oriented Python scripts to work with web API's, parse and format data scraped from websites, and store information into a multi-table MySQL database scheme that I designed.

projects.title: MITRE Hackathon: RFID Badge Security
projects.description: Investigated security of MITRE's RFID-enabled access badges. Won 2nd place out of 6 competing teams.

projects.title: MITRE Embedded Systems Capture the Flag Competition
projects.description:
A first-of-its-kind embedded hardware focused attack and defend style capture the flag competition. This project was an extended competition that lasted 7 weeks. The first three and a half weeks were spent designing and implementing a secure system to open a door upon reception of a correct passcode from the trusted device, a BeagleBone Black and an expansion board with cryptographic capabilities. In the second phase, we attacked another team's device and system.

We designed our system around RSA public key cryptography, encrypting and signing all messages between the device and the server. We used the TPM (Trusted Platform Module) on the device to hold keys and sign and encrypt messages.

In addition to the usual software attacks (brute force, keylogging, etc.), we also investigated a number of hardware attacks. For example, all communication with the chips on the expansion board is done over an I2C bus, so we attempted to replace an existing, unused chip with a microcontroller to spy on and potentially tamper with the I2C bus.
